Fable-Opus-Unit: lrapr-t1/t003-u3-flaky-gate-fix
Fable-Opus-Timeout-Minutes: 35

## Goal

Make the repository test gate `pnpm exec vp test --project node` reliable in /Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/versionless. The suite is currently 878/878 green when run alone but fails under parallel/contended load; the historical Codex run also recorded an 822/824 red. Known failure modes from a PM reproduction on 2026-08-10: (a) 5-second default test timeouts tripping on heavyweight integration tests — `packages/cli/test/next-killedbygoogle-integrate.test.ts` observed timing out, and `packages/cli/test/vite8-shared-adapter-cohort-run.test.ts` alone takes ~148s; (b) a hardcoded port collision — `Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:44210` from vite8-shared-adapter-cohort-run. Three further files failed in that contended run but were not identified.

Do this systematically, not just for the two named files:
1. Find every test that binds a fixed TCP port (grep the test and src trees for hardcoded port numbers / listen calls) and convert them to ephemeral allocation (bind port 0 and read the assigned port, or an equivalent existing project pattern) so concurrent runs cannot collide.
2. Find every test whose runtime can plausibly exceed the 5s default (long integration/witness/build tests) and give those tests or files explicit generous timeouts. Prefer per-test/per-file timeout configuration over raising the global default; if a global `testTimeout` bump in the vite/vp config is clearly the project's idiom, that is acceptable — say which you chose and why.
3. Prove stability: the full suite must pass twice consecutively.

This is a test-reliability change only: no product behavior changes, no assertion weakening, no test deletion or skipping.

## File contract

- `packages/cli/test/**`
- `packages/cli/src/**`
- `packages/core/test/**`
- `packages/frameworks/**/test/**`
- `vite.config.ts`

## Forbidden moves

- Do not weaken, delete, or skip any test or assertion. Why: the gate's meaning must not change; only its reliability.
- Do not change product runtime behavior except port-selection plumbing needed so tests can inject/observe an ephemeral port. Why: this unit must be a no-op for migration semantics.
- Do not touch evidence/**, fixtures/**, docs/goals/** or any file outside the contract. Why: curation is a later unit; the recovery snapshot floor is already sealed.
- Obey repo policy: strict TypeScript only, magic-regexp for regexes, pathe for paths, ufo for URLs.
- Do not touch the network.

## Verification

```verify
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm exec vp lint
pnpm exec vp test --project node
pnpm exec vp test --project node
```

## Blocked permission

If a fix genuinely requires files outside the contract, if a test's flakiness traces to a real product defect rather than timeouts/ports (report it — that changes the plan), or if the suite cannot pass twice consecutively after your changes, return status "blocked" with the exact failing output and question in open_questions instead of improvising.

All four verification commands are green. Summary of the work:

**Ports — every fixed TCP bind in the test and src trees is now ephemeral.** I swept `packages/*/src`, `packages/*/test` and `packages/frameworks/*` for `listen(`/hardcoded port literals. Nine fixture runners bound fixed ports; all now bind `0` and read the assigned port back through a local `ephemeralPort(server)` guard (`/Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/versionless/packages/cli/src/fixture/angular-phonecat-run.ts`, `angular-phonecat-composed-run.ts`, `angular-phonecat-route-resolve-run.ts`, `angular-phonecat-vite8-run.ts`, `react-boilerplate-v4-vite8-run.ts`, `react-boilerplate-v4-composed-run.ts`, `react-boilerplate-v4-data-flow-run.ts`). The two child-process servers (`react-boilerplate-v4-node24-run.ts`, `run.ts`) reserve an ephemeral port via a probe socket before spawning, since the port is passed as `PORT` env. The three `*PORT_PLAN` constants that produced the `EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:44210` collision are deleted, so the cohort's two profile orders can no longer collide with each other or with a second suite instance.

**The cohort test's port assertion got stronger, not weaker.** `packages/cli/test/vite8-shared-adapter-cohort-run.test.ts` previously asserted exact port values and pairwise disjointness. It now asserts, in the file's existing source-inspection idiom, that all three runner sources contain no hardcoded loopback port at all and do bind `0` with the ephemeral guard — collision-freedom by construction rather than by bookkeeping.

**Timeouts — global floor plus explicit per-test values.** I set `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout` to `120_000` on the node project in `vite.config.ts`, and raised the in-contract explicit `30_000` values to `300_000` (`dashboard-contacts-dependency-preflight.test.ts`, `witness-angular-contacts-run.test.ts`); the cohort's `900_000` stands. I chose the global bump deliberately: three of the PM's contended failures were never identified, so the flaky set is not enumerable from one machine's timings, and `packages/trust/test` and `packages/experiments/test` are in the same gate but outside my file contract — only a global floor protects them. A JSON-reporter run confirms the headroom is real: after the cohort's 147.4s, the next slowest test in the suite is 5.3s, so every non-cohort test now has 20x or better margin against the default.

One thing worth your attention, and the reason I stopped short of a clean sweep: `react-boilerplate-v4-data-flow-run.ts:417` still binds the fixed port 43440 for its service-worker upgrade server. That runner records `origin: http://127.0.0.1:43440` into `evidence/runs/react-boilerplate-v4-data-flow/artifacts/upgrade.json`, which is sealed and outside my contract. Making it ephemeral would make that artifact's digest vary per run and break the CLI's determinism verify — so this is a deliberate omission, not an oversight. It cannot affect the gate (no test invokes `verifyReactBoilerplateDataFlow`), but it will still collide if two CLI fixture runs execute concurrently, and closing it needs an evidence re-publish in a later unit.
